Three ways to count email and SMS

Monthly. Klaviyo’s own attribution credits any order placed within its window after an open or click (gross, includes first orders). Last click counts only orders where the final visit came from an email or SMS link (net, Lifetimely). The truth sits between them.

Does where they came from predict coming back?

Customers by the source of their first order: share who order again within a year, and first-year net value. Correlation, not cause: people who buy from an email were already subscribed and engaged.

Repeat within a yearRepeat within 90 days

Last 365 days, Klaviyo attribution (gross). Campaigns are one row; flows are automated. Flows that target existing customers are marked.

      Weekly gap since October 2025

      Below 1.0 means less was booked than Shopify recorded, common in launch and promo weeks before shipping catches up.

      ÷ Shopify net÷ Lifetimely net

      How the estimate is made: each day the finance system books about half of that day’s Lifetimely sales (product revenue less discounts) and the rest over the next six days as orders ship, and takes off most of the refunds from that day and the day before. The day weights are fitted on a year of daily booked figures, then scaled to match the last 30 days (—). Tested by month, it averaged 1.6% off what was booked.

      How the Nov + Dec forecast is built: new customers from the pre-peak run rate and a peak uplift between the last two years, returning customers from an active pool that is much bigger than last year.

      Model notes

      Net revenue is the finance system’s booked net sales. Lifetimely and Shopify feed the model; a daily bridge turns Lifetimely sales and refunds into the net revenue the finance system will book (Methodology › Net revenue bridge).

      Retail calendar. 4-5-4, Sunday to Saturday weeks. 2026 is FY27: 1 Feb 2026 to 30 Jan 2027.

      Customer pool. Every customer sits in a bucket by retail months since their last order. Each month each bucket buys at last year’s rate for that month; buyers return to bucket 1, new customers join it. Where last year’s rates come from before this year’s step up, a behaviour index of 1.043 (sales) and 1.035 (buyers) is applied; FY28 months use this year’s rates as they are.

      New customers. Oct +40% (current run rate). Nov and Dec +22%: the Sep + Oct level times a peak uplift halfway between FY25 (1.63×) and FY26 (2.10×). Jan +3.9%, as last January already sat after the step. FY28: +30% in February, fading evenly to +20% by October.

      From sales to net revenue. Forecast sales × last year’s same-month ratio of net revenue to sales (0.87 to 1.02), with a 1% drift for months whose ratio is from FY26.

      Customer data. Lifetimely orders since Oct 2021, guests excluded (16 orders). LTV is net revenue per customer (after discounts and returns, before tax). Gross margin in Lifetimely is unreliable, so LTV is not margin-based.

      Glossary

      Expected net revenueBooked where booked, estimated where Lifetimely has the day but the finance system does not yet, forecast for the rest.
      TargetThe weekly CA target from the trade workbook (Forecast sheet), loaded to W39.
      Active poolCustomers who ordered in the last 12 retail months.
      Net LTV (30, 90, 365 days…)Average net revenue per customer from the first order to that many days after it, counting only customers old enough.
      Repeat rateShare of new customers who place a second order within the window.
      Half-lifeDays by which half of the customers who will repeat within a year have done so.
      CohortCustomers grouped by the retail month of their first order.
      Win-back windowChance of an order in the next 90 days, given months since the last one.
      Due to buyCustomers expected to order in the next 30 days from their recency and order count.
      Cost per new customerGoogle and Meta spend in Lifetimely ÷ new customers. Excludes other paid channels and agency fees.
      Main itemThe highest-value line in an order; used to label the order’s category, department and brand.
